strategies.why: Growing the Poaceae family again and again lets its pests and diseases carry over (Poaceae family grown 2 time(s)). Sweet potato is from the Convolvulaceae family, so they lose their host for a season. The bare months get sesbania (Fabaceae), so the same family rarely follows itself.
changes: Grow sweet potato instead of rice once in the rotation
Add sesbania from mid-Sep to mid-Jan (also fits: okra, peanut, sunn hemp)
Add sesbania from mid-Apr to mid-Jun after rice (also fits: string bean, okra, mungbean)
benefits: Builds soil: the soil is covered more months; a legume adds nitrogen; deeper roots; a cover crop protects and feeds the soil (+62)
Less bare soil exposed to rain (+34)
Breaks pest and disease cycles with a different plant family (+80)
risks: Sweet potato needs well-drained soil; clay soil can stay wet after heavy rain
Heat of 35 °C+ is common while sesbania grows
Tight timing: sesbania needs 60+ days and the gap is about 60 days
More exposure to heat, frost, dry spells or flooding (-8)
gaps: FAO harvest statistics don't count cover crops, so we can't confirm that sesbania seed is sold near you
Crop values are national averages (FAOSTAT yields and farm-gate prices) before costs; your own yields and prices will differ
